decision_lens: The host-plugin contract is a trust boundary. Anything the host cannot enforce at compile time will eventually be violated by a third-party plugin developer. Document every assumption, enforce every invariant that can be enforced, and fail loudly when you can't.
distance_rationale: VST/AU plugin SDKs are platform substrates designed for first-class consumers (DAW plugins) with a stable multi-vendor API — structurally parallel to Palettice's consumer-supplied closure model — but in a domain where real-time budget, purity enforcement, and host-plugin trust boundaries are existential concerns that game-SDK designers typically discover only after shipping.
expected_isomorphisms: The VST 'process callback must be real-time safe (no allocation, no locking, no I/O)' invariant maps onto Palettice's DerivationFn purity requirement — both are consumer-supplied closures called on a hot path where violations are undetectable at compile time and produce subtle correctness bugs. The VST host's practice of `catch_unwind`-wrapping every plugin callback to isolate host from plugin panics is the direct transferable pattern for how Palettice should document derivation-closure panic policy.
focus: VST / AudioUnit / AAX audio plugin SDK host-plugin contract patterns applied to Palettice's consumer-supplied derivation closures, SoulStore trait ergonomics, and per-tick budget
name: fd-vst-plugin-host-contract
persona: A DAW plugin SDK engineer who has maintained a VST3 host implementation for five years and thinks reflexively about callback ownership, thread-safety contracts, real-time budget violations, and what happens when a plugin developer ignores the rules the SDK assumed they'd follow
review_areas: DerivationFn purity is underdocumented: §1 states 'Closures are pure functions; they MUST NOT have side effects' but this is a doc-comment convention with no enforcement; VST experience shows that plugin developers violate purity assumptions whenever it is convenient — allocating, locking, doing I/O; the spec should say explicitly what happens when a derivation is impure (non-deterministic caching, undefined replay behavior) and whether any lint/debug mode can detect violations

DerivationFn thread-safety contract: `DerivationFn = Arc<dyn Fn(...) + Send + Sync>` requires `Send + Sync` but derivations are called from `Soul::facet` / `Soul::derived` — the spec does not say which thread calls these or whether callers hold a `&mut Soul` lock; in a multi-threaded tick loop (fashionsomething, Solwend), concurrent reads of derived values from different threads could race on the `DerivedCache`

Missing derivation error propagation: `DerivationFn` returns `Option<FacetValue>` — `None` signals failure, but the caller gets no error message; §1 says mismatched derivations are 'errors at first read, not at construction' but the error type for a derivation returning `None` is nowhere specified; VST hosts require that plugin errors be distinguishable from 'no output' (a valid state)

Per-tick allocation budget: §9 observes that the naïve mood_system port allocates ~800 times/second for 8 elves; the spec recommends the derivation-based optimization but does not quantify the allocation budget or provide a zero-allocation path; VST real-time callbacks prohibit allocation entirely — Palettice is not real-time but elf-revel's 100-tick/sec loop is budget-sensitive

Plugin / consumer isolation: in VST, a buggy plugin cannot crash the host; in Palettice, a panicking derivation closure propagates up through `Soul::derived` and crashes the caller — the spec does not mention panic handling in closures; at minimum, the spec should document whether derivation closures are expected to be panic-free and whether `catch_unwind` wrapping is the consumer's responsibility

API surface for first-consumer vs. N-consumer stability: §5 `ScoringFormula` ships a `WeightedSum` variant tuned for fashionsomething and a `Custom` escape hatch; VST SDKs that ship a 'default preset' tuned for one host tend to create consumers who rely on undocumented behavior of that preset; the spec should call out which parts of `ScoringFormula::WeightedSum` are considered stable API vs. tuning parameters that may change

severity_examples.condition: A consumer derivation that performs a blocking I/O read (fetching a game asset) will stall `Soul::derived`, poison the cache with a value that cannot be invalidated, and produce non-deterministic replay; there is no debug-mode purity check and no documented way to detect this class of consumer error

If `Soul` is shared across threads (e.g. Solwend's async handlers reading the same Character-Soul from two concurrent requests), concurrent calls to `Soul::derived` may race on `DerivedCache::derived_at` — `Soul` does not implement `Sync` (and probably should not), but the spec does not state whether `Soul` is intended to be single-owner or shareable, leaving consumer threading models to guess
severity_examples.scenario: DerivedCache race condition in multi-threaded consumers

severity_examples.condition: A consumer derivation that panics on unexpected `FacetValue` shape (e.g. receiving `Unit` where it expected `Int`) propagates the panic through `Soul::derived` to the game tick loop, crashing the sim; the spec does not document panic policy or recommend `catch_unwind` at the derivation call site
severity_examples.scenario: Panicking derivation closure propagates to caller

source_domain: Audio / video plugin SDKs (VST3, AudioUnit, Avid AAX)
success_hints: The spec adds a sentence to the `DerivationFn` type alias documenting what 'no side effects' means in practice — no allocation beyond what the returned FacetValue requires, no I/O, no locking — and notes that a debug-mode wrapper can detect violations via allocation tracking
The `Soul` type's threading model is documented explicitly (single-owner in-memory value; not `Sync`; consumers who need shared access must use an `Arc<Mutex<Soul>>` or actor pattern)

DerivationFn returns `Result<Option<FacetValue>, DerivationError>` or the spec defines a separate `DerivationError` type so derivation failures are distinguishable from 'this derivation produced no value'
The spec calls out which `ScoringFormula::WeightedSum` fields are stable API vs. implementation detail subject to change
